# Agent Brief — Rules for Parallel Build Tracks

*Every build agent reads this first. It applies on top of `DEV_EXECUTION_PLAN.md` §4–§5. If this brief and a backlog row disagree, the row's acceptance criteria win for *what* to build and this brief wins for *how to behave*.*

## 1. Context in one paragraph
ANUMAAN (SIH 2026 PS-26054): AI-enabled real-time digital twin for health monitoring / fault prediction / mission reliability of aero piston engines on MALE UAVs (DRDO). One engine-agnostic codebase; profiles in `configs/engines/*.json` (Rotax 912iS/914/915iS, Austro AE300, VRDE/JAYEM 2.2 L). The plant (`backend/plant/virtual_engine.py`) is the independent simulated engine; everything that infers consumes canonical `Frame`s (`backend/core/frame.py`) and must never read ground truth. Already built: `backend/detect/` (calibration, scorers, conformal, gate, reservoir), `backend/runtime/` (EngineRuntime/RuntimeHub/registry/levers), `backend/server/engine_api.py`, `backend/edge/node.py`, `backend/sources/{plant_source,recorder}.py`, 275 tests. Frontend is **out of scope** (another track/later).

## 2. Read before coding (in order, skim what you do not need)
`docs/build/README.md` → `MENTAL_MODEL.md` → `DECISIONS.md` (D01–D37) → `INTERFACES.md` → `VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST.md` → `CURRENT_STATE.md` → the **BACKLOG rows for your track** and the design docs they cite (`docs/audit/09_full_depth_architecture.md`, `docs/audit/08_*`, `docs/audit/12_dataset_implementation.md`, etc.) → `SUPERSEDED_VS_CURRENT.md` (do not build on the superseded code) → `FINDINGS.md`.

## 3. Hard rules (violations get the work rejected)
1. **Truth isolation:** nothing under `backend/ml|twin|detect|sources|dsp|diagnosis|prognosis` may read `FAULT_ID/HEALTH_INDEX/RUL_HOURS` or `TruthRecord`; `tests/test_no_truth_leak.py` scans it (extend its directory list for new packages you create that infer).
2. **Engine-agnostic:** no `cyl`/brand/model literals in new code; derive from the `EngineConfig`/profile. `tests/test_engine_agnostic_ratchet.py` may only go **down** (never edit its baseline upward; new modules count if you add them to its list — add yours so they must stay at zero literals).
3. **Provenance & evidence:** every numeric constant that is not derived gets a label PUBLIC / MANUAL / ASSUMED / PLACEHOLDER in a docstring or config `provenance`; every reported result names its evidence class (SIMULATION / PUBLIC_PROXY / REAL_FLIGHT). Never quote simulator accuracy as field performance.
4. **No claim without a null control** (shuffled/random/baseline) and multiple seeds; report negative results as they are. Never tune on the test seeds; train/test seeds are disjoint (test offset ≥ 1000).
5. **No fabricated numbers, sources or licences.** If you cannot verify a fact (a public spec, a dataset property, a licence), write `UNVERIFIED` and add a verification row; do not fill in a plausible value. Third-party code/data needs a present, permissive licence (D35); check it and record it in your track note.
6. **Do not edit files you do not own** (see your prompt for ownership). Shared files — `docs/build/{BACKLOG,DECISIONS,FINDINGS,CURRENT_STATE,README,INTERFACES}.md`, `backend/runtime/*`, `backend/server/*`, `backend/core/*`, `backend/plant/virtual_engine.py` (unless your track owns it), `requirements.txt`, `tests/engine_agnostic_baseline.json`, `tests/test_no_truth_leak.py` — are edited **only by the integrator**. Instead write `docs/build/tracks/<TRACK>.md` (what you built, files, public API with signatures, tests, measured results with evidence class and seeds, honest limitations, findings, what the integrator must wire, requirements to add). New top-level packages are fine and encouraged.
7. **Library code in `backend/…`, never in experiment scripts.** Experiments go in `experiments/E<nn>_*.py` and write `docs/evaluation/E<nn>_*.json`; they call the library. Provide a `--quick` flag so tests can smoke them in seconds.
8. **Tests:** every module gets tests (`tests/test_<area>_*.py`), deterministic (seeded), each file < 30 s. Run `python -m pytest -q` for your files while working and the **full suite** at the end (~2.5 min; it must stay green — 275 pass + 1 xfail at branch point). No network in tests; skip (not fail) when an optional dataset is absent.
9. **Performance is a requirement:** anything on the live path must fit the 20 Hz × N engines budget; measure and record it (`time.perf_counter`), never call sklearn one row at a time on the hot path.
10. **Environment:** Windows 11, Git Bash + PowerShell, Python 3.12, NVIDIA GPU with CUDA torch available, Blender at `E:\Blender\blender.exe`. Large public datasets are in `E:\backup-llm\backup-no-llm\3d_engine\Datasets\` (read-only; NASA ACES in `data/telemetry/nasa_aces/`). You may `pip install` well-known permissive-licence libraries you need (e.g. ortools, pgmpy, filterpy); list them in your track note (the integrator adds them to `requirements.txt`). Do not download anything > 200 MB, do not call paid/cloud services, do not send data off the machine.
11. **Commit** only inside your worktree branch, in logical commits (`feat(<area>): …` + the standard `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` trailer). Never force-push, never touch `main`/`maverick-main`, never delete files outside your ownership.
12. **Scope discipline:** finish rows in dependency order; if a row proves too large, deliver the smaller honest version, mark the rest `NOT DONE` in your track note with the reason. A half-finished row presented as done is the worst outcome.

## 4. Definition of done for a row
Code + unit tests + (if it claims performance) an experiment JSON with seeds and null control + entry in your track note with *Verified* (what a test/experiment proves) and *Unproven* (what remains assumption) + full suite green.

## 5. Final report format (your last message)
Track name; branch name; rows DONE / PARTIAL / NOT DONE (one line each with the reason); files added (top-level list); test counts; headline measured numbers with evidence class; deviations from the backlog design and why; bugs found in existing code; requirements to add; exactly what the integrator must wire and where.
